thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: AZ-B synthetic healthchecks failing (route53 healthcheck errors) — 81% failures over last 3m. Auto-pager triggered to #eng-oncall (P2)
amanda: seeing the alerts. Is this widespread across customers or just internal probes?
raj: internal probes spike, but edge metrics show elevated 503s from our euw2-edge cluster that live in AZ-B. CPU looks normal.
lina: I can confirm increased 5xx from euw2 -> model-gateway in AZ-B. Latency +300ms for some requests.
miguel: checking route53 healthcheck logs now. Getting: "DNS timeout" for healthcheck target from us-east probes. Could be cross-region resolver issues.
amanda: can someone check the Route53 healthcheck region set? maybe probes are being blocked or misrouted.
raj: running quick curl from a bastion in AZ-B: `curl -v http://10.4.12.7:8080/health` -> hangs then `Connection timed out`.
lina: same from container exec on gateway: `kubectl exec -n gateway -c probe gw-42 -- curl -sS 10.4.12.7:8080/health` -> nothing. Pod seems up per kubectl.
miguel: pulling node-level networking: `ip route` looks fine. I'm seeing a flurry of ICMP unreachable from one rack switch. Tagging networking team.
sre-lead: switching to mitigation mode — we need to avoid noisy auto-failovers. Step 1: suspend automated Route53 failover for affected records to prevent oscillation. Step 2: reduce synthetic probe frequency (debounce) while we investigate.
amanda: agree. ops-bot, please disable healthcheck policy `euw2-azb-synth` (temporarily) and scale down frequency to 1/5.
ops-bot: Command received. Disabling `euw2-azb-synth` and setting interval to 300s. (changes applied) :white_check_mark:
raj: i've opened a ticket with the colo provider for the switch logging (ticket #COL-8721). They show a brief control-plane maintenance window at the time failures started.
lina: customer impact? Any production 4xx/5xx surfaced to customers?
amanda: early panics: certain EU customers on regional routing saw increased retries (15-20% elevated error rates for ~8 minutes). Not global.
miguel: cross-region routing: automatic fallback sent some traffic to us-west-2 which increased latency there by 80ms for affected sessions. No model inference errors reported.
sre-lead: next steps: 1) keep synth probes suppressed, 2) monitor gateway request success rate and scale if needed, 3) if colo can't confirm quick fix, plan manual DNS failover to eu-central backup pool.
carol: do we need to hit the incident channel for exec? P2 but customer visible.
amanda: I don't think exec notif yet — this is limited. We'll update status page if we do manual DNS change.
raj: putting a short post in status: "Partial regional reachability issue in AZ-B; engineering investigating. Some customers may see transient errors"
incident-bot: PagerDuty: oncall amanda acknowledged at 2109876560.
raj: I've collected tcpdump from gateway (saved to s3://rdw-debug/euw2/2109876570.tgz).
miguel: colo responded — control-plane maintenance caused a temporary ACL rule to go into a default-deny for a handful of leaf switches, they reverted at 2109876800.
lina: after revert, probes recovered but we still see intermittent flaps for 3-4 minutes. Could be leftover ARP cache entries.
sre-lead: flush ARP on affected nodes and drain any hot connections that are stuck. Use `ip -s -s neigh flush all` on nodes in pool.
amanda: running ARP flush on two nodes now.
ops-bot: ARP flush command issued across nodes in euw2-gateway-pool.
raj: post-flush metrics look good. 5xx back to baseline, latency returning to normal.
miguel: storage of tcpdump shows retransmits during the window — will attach to incident ticket.
carol: great. Who's owning the postmortem and action items?
sre-lead: I'll own the postmortem. Action items: (1) make synthetic probe debounce default for multi-AZ failures, (2) add ARP/neighbor flush automation to our recovery playbook, (3) coord with colo for change windows and pre-notify, (4) add a Route53 failover cool-down timer to prevent oscillation.
amanda: i'll draft the customer-impact blurb for status page and coordinate comms.
oncall-next: i'll take handoff at 2109880000 — will monitor for the next hour and validate that Route53 configs remain steady.
raj: handing off notes to @oncall-next (see s3 logs and ticket #COL-8721).
oncall-next: acknowledged. Will escalate to networking if flaps resume.
incident-bot: Incident P2 transitioned to monitoring at 2109876950; severity de-escalated.
sre-lead: logging follow-up tasks in Jira: RINF-1292 (probe-debounce), RINF-1293 (ARP-automation), RINF-1294 (route53-cooldown).
amanda: thanks team. I'll post an initial incident summary in #incidents in 30m with impact numbers (estimated ~12% of EU sessions saw transient errors for ~8m).
carol: :thumbsup: nice work.
